day1.subject: one system instead of five
day1.body:
Tomislav, you are running SEO and analytics for an agency working across five offices in three countries, which is the point where reporting stops being a spreadsheet job and starts being a resourcing problem.

The question I would put to you is how long it takes to see which client work actually made money last month. Most agency leads at that size can tell me revenue quickly and margin per project slowly, because the hours live in one place and the invoices in another.

Is that the shape of it at Meridian, or have you already solved it?

day1.subject: utilisation across four delivery teams
day1.body:
Luka, you are running delivery operations across four teams and a hundred and twenty people, which is the size where capacity planning stops fitting in a spreadsheet and starts costing you real margin.

The question I would put to you is how far ahead you can see resourcing. Most operations leads at that headcount can tell me who is busy this week and have no reliable answer for the month after next, so the first sign of a problem is a project that has already gone over.

How are you handling that at Lumen today?

context: trial ran properly, died on the minimum commitment

diagnosis.died_because: died on the upfront minimum, not the unit rate
